newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks take battering on baht, politics.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks take battering on baht, politics.

text.p: Thai stocks took a further battering on Tuesday as the weakness of the baht combined with domestic political worries sent the market to a six-week low, brokers said.
The SET Index ended 13.90 points, or 2.30 percent lower, at 590.44 on trade worth 2.712 billion baht. The SET 50 fell 1.24 points, or 2.73 percent, to close at 44.12.
The baht weakness was a key contributor to bearish sentiment as the currency sank to a near record low of 32.68 to the dollar onshore, traders said.
The mood was further dampened by political concerns over infighting in the dominant New Aspiration Party and an upcoming parliamentary vote on a new constitution, analysts said.
"This all points to more weakness in the market, I don't see any bright news at the moment," said Mike Stead, head of research at Union Securities.
Communications stocks lost 5.05 percent on poor earnings fears and reports that some firms were cutting staff wages, traders said.
Finance stocks ended off lows but still lost 1.03 percent. A central bank news conference in the afternoon did not produce any fresh bad news for the finance sector, traders said.
Bangkok Bank lost two baht to 158, Dhana Siam shed 1.50 to 29.75, Advanced Info 13 to 195.
